Event: Star of South Africa diamond discovered (83.5 carats)
Notes: Triggered diamond rush in South Africa

Event: Cecil Rhodes arrives in South Africa
Notes: Aged 16; later joins diamond fields

Event: Diamonds discovered at Vooruitzigt farm
Notes: Later site of Big Hole mine

Event: Cecil Rhodes enters Kimberley diamond fields
Notes: Aged 18; manages brother's mining claims

Event: Cecil Rhodes meets Charles Rudd
Notes: Begin diamond mining partnership

Event: Diamond fields depression period
Notes: Rhodes and Rudd consolidate interests; obtain water pump contract

Event: De Beers Consolidated Mines formed
Notes: Merger of Rhodes and Barnato companies; financed by N.M. Rothschild & Sons; £200

Event: Strategic partnership with London Diamond Syndicate
Notes: Agreement to regulate output and maintain prices; De Beers gains near-monopoly

Event: De Beers monopoly sealed
Notes: De Beers controls 90% of world diamond supply

Event: Trade slump - supply curtailed to maintain prices
Notes: Diamond Syndicate restricts supply to support prices

Event: Cecil Rhodes' term as Cape Colony PM ends
Notes: After Jameson Raid failure; continued involvement with De Beers

Event: Diamonds discovered near Pretoria
Notes: Leads to Premier Mine discovery

Event: Cullinan Diamond found at Premier Mine
Notes: Largest rough diamond ever discovered; Cullinan refuses to join De Beers cartel

Event: Cecil Rhodes dies
Notes: Age 48; De Beers controls 90% of world production

Event: Diamonds discovered in German South West Africa
Notes: Ernest Oppenheimer becomes agent for London Syndicate

Event: Ernest Oppenheimer appointed mayor of Kimberley
Notes: Rises to prominence; emphasizes scarcity value of diamonds

Event: Ernest Oppenheimer joins De Beers board
Notes: Previously founded Anglo American mining company

Event: Ernest Oppenheimer becomes De Beers chairman
Notes: Consolidates global monopoly over diamond industry

Event: Experimental work on diamond drills
Notes: Pioneering use of diamond drills; enables Free State Gold Rush

Event: US Justice Department files antitrust case against De Beers
Notes: Response to wartime attempts to negotiate Sherman Act exemption

Event: Frances Gerety coins "A Diamond is Forever" slogan
Notes: For N.W. Ayer & Son advertising campaign; becomes most successful 20th century slogan

Event: De Beers opens new combined Anglo American headquarters
Notes: Integrates Anglo American and De Beers operations

Event: Ernest Oppenheimer dies; Harry Oppenheimer takes over
Notes: Continues monopoly; expands to multiple countries

Event: De Beers market dominance peak
Notes: De Beers controls 80-85% of rough diamond distribution

Event: Anglo and De Beers account for major South African economic output
Notes: 10% of South Africa's GNP and 30% of country's exports

Event: De Beers forced to divest American assets
Notes: To avoid Sherman Antitrust Act violation

Event: Harry Oppenheimer steps down as chairman
Notes: Ends era of direct Oppenheimer leadership

Event: De Beers market dominance period
Notes: Controls up to 90% of world diamond supply

Event: Global Witness campaign on blood diamonds
Notes: Triggers UN investigation into conflict diamonds

Event: De Beers stops all outside diamond buying
Notes: De Beers market control drops to 63% (from 90%)

Event: De Beers business model changes
Notes: Response to competition from Canada and Australia; blood diamond concerns

Event: Kimberley Process Certification Scheme created
Notes: Sets requirements for controlling rough diamond production and trade

Event: De Beers pleads guilty to industrial diamond price fixing
Notes: Pays $10 million fine for 1994 collusion with General Electric

Event: De Beers uses blockchain to track diamonds
Notes: Successfully tracks 100 high-value diamonds from mine to retailer

Event: De Beers launches Lightbox synthetic diamond brand
Notes: Lab-grown diamonds at $200-$800 per carat

Event: Oppenheimer family sells 40% stake to Anglo American
Notes: Sale for £3.2 billion ($5.1 billion); ends 80-year Oppenheimer dynasty

Event: De Beers pays $295 million class-action settlement
Notes: Price fixing accusations; appealed but ultimately paid

Event: De Beers market share continues to decline
Notes: Market share drops from 90% (1980s) to 29.5%

Event: De Beers launches Tracr blockchain traceability platform
Notes: End-to-end traceability from mine to store

Event: Lab-grown diamonds 90% cheaper than mined diamonds
Notes: Lab-grown prices at ~10% of mined diamonds; Lightbox brand discontinued

Event: Anglo American announces intention to spin off or sell De Beers
Notes: De Beers currently owned 85% by Anglo American; 15% by Botswana

Event: De Beers holds $2 billion in unsold mined diamonds
Notes: Decline in demand for natural diamonds; lab-grown competition
